summary: Uric acid is produced when the body breaks down purines from food and from its own cells. When it exceeds what stays dissolved, crystals form in joints, which is gout.
what_it_measures: The concentration of urate in blood, reported in micromol/L.

interpretations.meaning: A raised urate increases the risk of gout and urate kidney stones. Many people with a raised level never develop symptoms, so it is not treated on the number alone.

when_to_seek_help: A hot, swollen, exquisitely painful joint needs assessment — urate levels can be normal during an acute gout attack, so the diagnosis is clinical.
approved_by: Demo dataset (illustrative values, not for clinical use)
